correctness.rationale: For equal-trace 2x2 Hermitians A=aI+v·σ and B=aI+w·σ, Pauli operator norm of a difference is |scalar|+|vector|. Spectral calculus gives |A|=(|a|,sgn(a)v) for r=|v|<=|a| and (r,(a/r)v) for r>|a|. On the outer region, derivative restricted to v changes has gain sqrt(1+a²/r²) (radial and tangent directions); inner region gain one. Integration along every chord, splitting at at most two sphere crossings, yields <=sqrt2 globally when a!=0 and strict below sqrt2 for each distinct pair, since equality of outer derivative is possible only on rank-one boundary points of measure zero. A near-boundary radial-plus-transverse directional witness approaches sqrt2; at a=0, |A|=|v|I so reverse triangle proves attained constant 1. Independently calculated 3200 input-pair ratios and three approaching gains 1.4004,1.4128,1.41407. The finite examples are corroboration, not general proof.
